finding.text: Ask 4, the cross-family review, is not done. Nobody has run `Server/review.mjs --model <openrouter slug>` on a real recent task and compared it with the same-model review. task.jsonl:1 lists it only as a planned step, and the diff adds just a comment at Server/review.mjs:666. That comparison is the owner's second reason for this work (a consensus from other model families), so it has to run before the task lands.

The real cost usually comes out as $0. Billing on OpenRouter takes a few seconds to settle, and `refresh_or_cost()` (Agents.js:1091) reads the key total right when the turn ends. So each turn shows the previous turn's spend, and the last turn's spend never shows at all; a one-shot reviewer would show $0. spike.jsonl:739 already shows this: deepseek's total is $0 for two real turns. Re-read the total a few seconds after the turn ends, or poll until it changes, so that the dashboard shows the real cost as ask 2 requires.

The spike's cost-per-turn result can't be trusted for the same reason: four of its six rows report $0 for a turn that did work. Add a short wait before each `key_usage()` read in spike.mjs (lines 666 and 676), then re-run the spike once so ask 1's "cost per turn" has real numbers.

The "id never matches" conclusion is wrong. spike.jsonl:743 (gemini-3.8-flash) has `generation_id_matches_message_id: true`, but the minion's log (wire-provider/task.jsonl:795) and the readme say it never matches. Where the id does match, `generation_cost()` returns an exact per-turn figure that doesn't depend on the shared key total. Worth a second look before settling on the before/after diff.

The tiers.js comment at line 180 says "Agents.spawn() already reads this `provider` field", which isn't true. Roles take only `model(tier)` (roles.js:21), and spawn picks the provider by the slash rule on the model id. The new `provider` export (tiers.js:190) has no callers. It works anyway, because an OpenRouter slug always contains a `/`. Either make the comment say that, or have roles copy the tier's `provider` too.

Nothing prevents `provider: "openrouter"` with a `claude-*` model. That would bill Claude per token through the gateway, which requirements.md rules out ("Claude itself stays on the subscription"). A one-line refusal in `Agents.spawn()` (Agents.js:107) would enforce the rule.

Some of the readme is out of date now. Point 2 (Servex/ext/openrouter/readme.md:14) still says "nothing reads" the provider field, and point 3 (readme.md:17) says "OpenRouter puts the real dollar cost on every reply", which contradicts the key-total diff that was actually built. Both should match what the code does now.

Simpler: `real_cost()` in provider.js has no callers, and `has_key()`'s comment says door() uses it, which it doesn't (only spike.mjs does). Delete the dead export and fix the comment. Also, `COST_CAP_USD` in spike.mjs:573 is only reported, never enforced; the only real cap is `maxTurns`.

Asks 1–3 are otherwise met. GPT, DeepSeek and Gemini Flash each completed Read, Bash and Edit, with streaming and a working resume. The provider can be set per spawn and is kept on resume, and the Gemini `ArtifactData` schema 400 was correctly worked around with `disallowedTools`. Compaction through the proxy has not been tested yet; it stays an open question in the readme.

The spend guard must come before OpenRouter spawns (requirements 2.1): Agents.js:100–115 in diff.patch accepts them without a daily cap, and spike.mjs:571–574 merely reports a $0.25 cap after both turns. A costly or looping turn can consume the owner's credit before that check.

The dashboard cost is not reliably real (requirements 1.2 and 2.1): Agents.js:125–155 in diff.patch reads the shared key total immediately at turn end without waiting for billing or isolating concurrent agents. spike.jsonl:739 reports $0 for two successful DeepSeek turns; a final turn's late charge may never appear on its agent.
The cross-family comparison is missing (requirement 1.4): Server/review.mjs:666–669 in diff.patch adds only a comment; there is no recorded run on a recent task alongside a same-model review.

The phase-two evaluation is absent from this patch (requirements 2.2–2.5 and 2b): it contains no known-answer rule tests, effort-level cost table, model-by-task matrix, probe-result log, or brainstorm-and-rate naming run. The Read/Bash/Edit spike tests SDK compatibility, not whether agents follow this project's rules or build a working page.

A tier's provider is not actually the switch (requirement 1.2): tiers.js:190 in diff.patch exports `provider`, but the patch has no caller for it; Agents.js:35 chooses by model slash instead. Moving a tier's provider alone therefore does nothing; either pass it from role defaults or describe the slash rule as the sole switch.

The spike mislabels a failed resume as a pass (requirement 1.1): spike.mjs:719–729 prints `resume ok` from `!is_error` without checking the answer; spike.jsonl:743 has an empty Gemini Flash resume answer marked successful. Verify that the response names red and blue before counting it.

An explicit `provider: "openrouter"` can be paired with a Claude model in Agents.js:35 of diff.patch, contrary to requirements.md:13 that Claude stay on the subscription. Refusing that combination is simpler than relying on every caller to remember the billing boundary.

provider.js:321–330 in diff.patch exports `real_cost()` but Agents.js implements a separate key-difference calculation; use one cost path. The readme's claims at lines 426–431 also still describe the provider field as unread and real cost as attached to every reply, unlike the patch.

The task's own Test library page names three tests that don't exist ("new-page-glossary", "plan-counter", and the old `evals/library/` folder, which `tests/page.js` says is gone), and its links go to dead `#` anchors and to `github.com/search` (content 7, 8) — diff, `test-library/page.js` lines 28–36; shots/…-test-library/1200.png, band 2. It should link to [/framework/ai/tests/](/framework/ai/tests/) and name the five real tests: h1-page, fix-label, broken-import, broken-overflow, plan-views.

Nothing links to [/framework/ai/tests/](/framework/ai/tests/). `public/framework/ai/page.js` `children:` doesn't name `tests`, and the diff doesn't add it, so you can only reach the library by typing its URL (page 5).

Phase 7 asked for a daily cap that matches the $50/month pace (about $1.50 a day, and $10 a week shown on the dashboard). The readme gives `SERVEX_OR_DAILY_CAP` a default of $8 a day (`Servex/ext/openrouter/readme.md:94`). Also, `spend.json` shows a total of $69.47, which is more than the $50 credit. Either the cap was never enforced, or that total mixes the SDK's Claude-priced estimates with OpenRouter's real cost (spike.jsonl has `cost_sdk_usd` 0.31 vs `real_cost_usd` 0.007). Say which one it is, on the dashboard.
Two pages carry the same title, "Test library": /framework/ai/tests/ and the task's test-library/ page (content 7). They also describe the library differently ("Five small tasks" vs "Small tasks").

The plan-views run pages (opus, fable) show "404 — nothing matches", because a planning run writes a page.jsonl and no page.js — shots/…-runs-plan-views-fable-…/1200.png. Either give planning runs a page, or stop shooting them.

The library index's previews are bare titles with no description, and the weights line is tiny muted text that reads "n/a" for most tests. The page is 73–92% empty at every width (layout.json `empty`) — shots/…-ai-tests/sheet.png.

Each test page opens with "confidence 0.00 · weight 0 · discrimination n/a — fewer than 4 models have run this". A newcomer reads three zeros before seeing the prompt — shots/…-ai-tests-h1-page/1200.png, band 1.

The "Test library runs" page is 2 lines of text on an empty screen, and its own comment says it is "never browsed directly". It could list its run folders as a wall instead — shots/…-test-library-runs/sheet.png.

Two test libraries exist side by side (requirements phase 3 "a test library"; CLAUDE.md law 6; content 7). The [test-library page](/framework/ai/2026-09-30/openrouter-harness/test-library/) still lists five *different* tests (new-page-glossary, plan-counter…) under `Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/library/`. Meanwhile [/framework/ai/tests/](/framework/ai/tests/) lists H1 page, Fix label, Broken import, Broken overflow and Plan views, and says that folder "is gone". Evidence: shots/…-test-library/1920.png, band 2, against shots/…-framework-ai-tests/1920.png. Point the old page at /framework/ai/tests/, or retire it.

A run the spend cap refused still shows as a model FAIL (phase 11, pass rate). `tests/h1-page/page.jsonl` line 16 records `openai/gpt-6-luna` with `pass: 0` and the note "spawn refused: today's OpenRouter spend ($7.65) is at or over the $1.5/day cap". library.mjs now skips these runs (diff.patch ~line 368), but the line already written was never removed. So the H1 page's pass rate and its runs table still count a model that never ran.

Every test page logs a 404 on load (page 6; smoke-test rule "loads with no console errors"). layout.json `errors` holds "Failed to load resource … 404" at all four widths on /framework/ai/tests/ and on all five test pages. The tests' own floor check is "no console error", so the pages that define the check fail it.

The spend log shows the day's OpenRouter spend reached $7.65 against a $1.50/day cap (phase 7) before the guard refused spawns. The cap does stop new spawns, but it allowed about five times the daily pace first. Worth one line in gaps.md.

Criteria lists show backticks as literal text (CLAUDE.md trap: only `p()`/`h1`–`h6` read backticks). On shots/…-tests-h1-page/1920.png, "What a good run does" shows `` `new Page({ meta: import.meta, … })` `` and `` `children:` `` with the backtick characters visible. Fix it in AITest.js `li(c)`.

On a test page, the result comes last (page 3; flow 25). The runs table, which shows which model passed, sits below the prompt and criteria. At 1920 it starts at the bottom edge of the screen (shots/…-tests-h1-page/1920.png, "Runs · 5"). Move the pass rate and the runs table above the prompt.

The index cards show titles only (page 10). Each test's weight is printed as tiny muted text in a separate block below the cards, using slugs (`fix-label: 0`) rather than the card titles. Put the weight and pass rate on each card instead. At 3440 the page is 92% empty (layout.json `empty` 0.915).

The runs index explains itself and then lists nothing (page 9). shots/…-test-library-runs/1920.png is one paragraph on an 89%-empty screen. Each run folder loads by URL, but no page lists the runs, so a run is reachable only from a test's table. The two plan-views run URLs are 404 error pages (layout.json errors), because a planning run writes markdown, not a page.js.

The runs table is squeezed into the reading column, so its right-hand columns are cut off. At 1920 the "$" column shows only a sliver and the judge's note is cut mid-word, while about 900px of the screen to the right stays empty (layout 6, flow 26). Evidence: shots/…-ai-tests-h1-page/1920.png, runs band. At 400 the table is cut after "pass" (400.png), so score, credit and cost can't be seen. Cost per run is the number this whole task exists to show.

The weights line on the Test library index runs the entries together: "h1-page: 0fix-label: 0broken-import: 0…". Each entry is a `small()` with no separator. It also shows `0` for every test, while each test's own page says the weight "is measured once 4 models have run it". One page shows a measurement and the other says there isn't one yet (page 8, words 7). Evidence: shots/…-ai-tests/1920.png, the band below the cards; public/framework/ai/tests/page.js, `small(`${r.slug}: ${r.weight}`)`.

Every recorded run is at `low` effort. Phase 9 and phase 10 say to start every model at MEDIUM thinking and treat that as the default sample (Requirements, phases 9 and 10). Evidence: every run folder name ends in `-low-`, and so does routing.json's `"effort": "low"`.

In the live page, the "note" column has been pushed past the table's edge. The cells left over are narrow, so each row grows to about 300px tall, and four runs fill more than a screen. Evidence: a fresh headless shot of /framework/ai/tests/h1-page/ at 1920. Fix 1 fixes this too.

The criteria list shows backticks as literal characters, as in "`new Page({ meta: import.meta, … })`". Only `p()` and `h1`–`h6` read backticks, and the criteria go through `li()` (code/css, CLAUDE.md traps). Evidence: the live headless shot, "What a good run does".

The index's test cards show a title only, with no one-line description of what each test asks. At 1200 "Plan views" sits alone on a second row (page 8, layout 11). Evidence: shots/…-ai-tests/1200.png and 1920.png.
The "reasoning" column is empty on every row. Hide it until a run fills it (page 9). Evidence: shots/…-ai-tests-h1-page/1920.png.

Each keys-to-success page opens with the raw dictated prompt, and the answer the page exists to show (the consensus keys and each model's score) sits below it, one to three screens down (page 1, presentation rule "level 1 shown, detail nested"). Evidence: `shots/…keys-to-success-research-process-fast-assistants/1920.png`, where the prompt fills the whole first screen. layout.json gives the page-keys-test band a share of 3.59 at 400 and 2.75 at 1920. Fix: put the keys and the score table first, and move the prompt below them or into a collapsed block.

The keys-to-success index and its child pages use the URL slug as their title: "bigger", "unsupported-link", "research-process-fast-assistants". Their sibling tests have real names, like "H1 page" and "Broken import" (words: names can't be misread). The index cards carry no description either, so a reader can't tell what any prompt is about without opening it. Evidence: `shots/…keys-to-success/1200.png`, the preview wall. In the diff, line 1 of each page.jsonl reads `"title":"bigger"`.

The slug titles also wrap to two lines on most child pages at 400, and on two of them at every width. layout.json reports `h1.page-title` at 2 lines on cards-and-logs-subdomain and research-process-fast-assistants at 1200, 1920 and 3440. A short plain-words title fixes this together with finding 2.

The Test library index preview for "Keys to success" is the only card with a description, so it stands taller than the five tests beside it. Evidence: `shots/…framework-ai-tests/1920.png`, top band. Giving every test a one-line description, or none, would make the wall even.

The 12 `test-library/runs/h1-page-*` shots are fixtures that models wrote during the tests. Most show an empty "Floor test" page: layout.json gives page-previews a share of 0 and 85–94% of the screen is empty. That is expected for a test fixture. They are not pages for readers, so their design was not judged.
The `drawer-rail` and `mode-btn` buttons wrap (1.7–3.2 lines) on every page, at every width. That comes from the shared site chrome, not from this diff.
